5.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 2082

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 679, (Omnibus No. 60 —Various Housekeeping
           Items), Bylaw No. 2082, 2023"

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2082 at 7:47 p.m.

            Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that The City of Langford is proposing to
           amend Zoning Bylaw No. 300 in the following ways:
           • By introducing regulations with respect to tandem parking in townhouse
           developments;
           • By increasing the width of interior, or in-garage, parking spaces;
           • By introducing "accessory dormitories which may include a kitchenette" as a permitted
           use in the CD2 (Hull's Field) zone;
           • By restricting where apartments may occur at the ground level in the City Centre
           Pedestrian (CCP) zone to exclude Peatt Road, Claude Road, Bryn Maur Avenue, Jacklin
           Road and Veterans Memorial Parkway;
           • By deleting the requirement for a lm wide landscaping strip adjacent to an interior
           side
           lot line in the City Centre 1 (CC1) zone.
           • By consolidating all daycare capacity exemptions from each zone into Part 3 of the
           Zoning

      bylaw.
      • By allowing R2 (One-and Two-family Residential) lots to be less than 600m2 but not
      less
      than 500m2 if the lot width is 17m.
      • By prohibiting landscape retaining walls that are visitable from municipal roads that
      are
      finished as smooth concrete blocks and/or a natural concrete colour.
      AND
      • By introducing requirements for accessible parking in all types of multi-family
      residential
      development.
      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
      Act.

      Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

      B. Armstrong, Rodney Rd - Expressed concern with the deletion of the requirement for a
      lm wide landscaping strip adjacent to an interior side lot line in the City Centre 1 (CC1)
      zone.

      Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presenters.

      None presented.

      Mayor Goodmanson declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2082 closed at 7:52 pm.

5.2   BYLAW NO. 2099

      "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 693, (971 Walfred Road) Bylaw No. 2099,
      2023".

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2099 at 7:52 p.m.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Pat Guiney has applied on behalf of
      1157393 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 971 Walfred Road from the One- and Two-
      Family Zone to the Residential Townhouse 1 Zone.


      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 13
      townhouses.


      Prior to Public Hearing, the applicant has provided a technical memo from an engineer
      that verifies stormwater can be adequately managed on-site for the proposed
      development, which has been approved by the Director of Engineering AND a memo by
      a Landscape Architect that examines existing trees on site and along the frontages to
      provide comment on potential tree retention, which has been approved by the Director
      of Planning.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:
1. Amenity Contributions as a bonus for increased density as follows:
a. $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b. $3,660 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.


2. Road dedication, full frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan, and a
construction parking plan — all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;


3. Onsite paver stones, an arbour with a pedestrian gate, and variable rooflines — all to
the satisfaction of the Director of Planning;


4. That storage within garages does not prevent parking of vehicles, tree protection
measures are carried out throughout the entire construction period, and that concrete
used will comply with Council's Low Carbon Concrete Policy;


5. With respect to the neighbouring property at 3303 Lodmell, the developer will install
drainage improvements, remove the existing retaining wall, install a 6-foot fence along
the shared property line, retain trees along the shared property line, and plant an
additional 8 tree along the shared property line.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'Neighbourhood'
designation.


Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
Act.

Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

Pat Guinev, Applicant - expressed support for the proposed development and provided
an overview of some energy efficient features of the build including solar energy, electric
car chargers, heat pumps, electric water heaters and induction cook tops. Speaker also
concerned about parking in the area, noting visitor spots including oversized parking
that will be accessible.

Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

D. Knudson, Lodmell Rd - expressed concerns with the proposed development including
changes to the neighbourhood over time, effects of previous developments have had on
the speaker's property, and proposed possible remedies for Council's consideration.

L. Plomp, Whimfield Terr - expressed support for the proposed development including
extensive public engagement undertaken by the applicant, and addressing of close
proximity resident's concerns.

Mendez, Mesa PI - expressed concern with the proposed development including concern
for safety of children and pedestrians in the area, size of the proposed buildings, and
emergency safety considerations.

M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - expressed support for the proposed development including the
applicants work in the community previously.

J.Patterson, Lodmell Rd - expressed concerns with parking within and nearby the
proposed development and concern for safety of children and pedestrians in the area.

Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presenters.

Councillor Wagner inquired to the Engineering Department. What is the current parking
situation near the proposed development?

K.Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded - there is currently no
visitor parking on Lodmell Rd, only on Walfred Rd. Parking issues, should they arise, will
be monitored by the Bylaw Enforcement Department. No parking or limited parking
signage would be erected if necessary.

Councillor Wagner inquired to the Engineering Department. Is the current parking there
scalloped?

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded confirming the scalloped
parking style on Walfred Rd.

Councillor Szpak inquired to staff and Council. Regarding the neighbour at 3303 Lodmell
Rd who has been experiencing difficulties, what can be done to mitigate these issues?

M. Baldwin, Director of Planning responded - staff included the owners of 3303 Lodmell
Rd's concerns as conditions of zoning.

Councillor Szpak wished to confirm that the conditions of zoning as presented were
amenable to the owner of 3303 Lodmell Rd.

D. Knudson, Lodmell Rd - responded confirming these conditions are satisfactory.

Councillor Harder inquired to the Engineering Department. Based off the traffic safety
comments, it appears that the landscaping plans show a sheltered area with pavers and
a bench for those waiting for the bus. Preferably, this is landscaped like the rest of
Walfred Rd.

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded confirming the bench and
shelter will be present with a 2.2m sidewalk that connects to the existing ones on
Walfred Rd as well as a stop sign on Lodmell Rd.

Councillor Harder noted appreciation for comments regarding families reducing to one
vehicle.

Mayor Goodmanson inquired to the Engineering and Public Works Department. Is the
parking on Walfred signed for use by this development or is it for anyone?

K. Balzer, Director of Engineering and Public Works responded confirming the parking
spots are for the public.

             Mayor Goodmanson declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2099 closed at 8:18 pm.

6.   PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

     Councillor Harder left the meeting at 8:18 p.m.

     Mayor Goodmanson opened the public participation period.

     Councillor Harder returned to the meeting at 8:19 p.m.

     S. Perry, Glen Lake Rd — re: item 4.1— Speaker expressed opposition to the City joining the CRD
     Arts and Culture Program noting Langford and Victoria do not share a border. Speaker also
     encouraged the City to plan for an arts and culture space within the new university building.
     Speaker expressed a wish for Langford's money to stay within the municipality. Speaker
     expressed concern for safety within the City of Victoria and cautioned Council against providing
     funding. re: item 4.2 —Speaker expressed concern with electric water heating tanks noting costs
     associated with this feature including insurance and replacement. Speaker also noted electric
     water heating tanks occupy a large amount of space.

     J. Withers, Woodhampton Rise — re: item 4.1 — Speaker expressed support for the City joining
     the CRD Arts and Culture Program noting a need to travel into Victoria currently to experience
     live music and a wish to have this form of entertainment locally. Speaker noted that music
     fosters a sense of community and local identity.

     J. Rye, Finney Rd — re: item 13.1 — Speaker attempted to address an item that was the subject of
     a previous Public Hearing. As a result, the speaker was interrupted and their comments
     disallowed.

     S. Sifert, Walfred Rd — re: 9.1.7 Speaker expressed concern with the report noting that
     homelessness and camping in public spaces cause negative impacts to residents and businesses.
     Speaker noted that shelters are appearing in many places throughout the City and consideration
     of residents and business safety is important.

     R. Louie, Bellamy Rd — re: item 4.1 —Speaker expressed opposition to the City joining the
     program as there is no opt out feature. Speaker also noted that Langford organizations are not
     guaranteed to receive funding from the program and if they do, it may not be proportionate.
     Speaker noted that the funding should stay within the community and the funding rates through
     the CRD may increase in the future.

     M. Morton, Phelps Ave — re: item 13.5 —Speaker expressed concern with the Tree Bylaw noting
     that homeowners and residents of Langford are experiencing issues with the Bylaw including
     adverse financial effects and unfair process.

     M. Wignall, 2375 Selwyn Rd — re: item 4.1 —Speaker expressed concern with the costs of the
     CRD Arts and Culture program noting the City may not receive the value for the money invested.
     re: item 13.7 —Speaker expressed concern with sheltering within the City, noting the difficult
     relationship between enforcement and allowing sheltering to occur from a public safety
     perspective.

     W. Bowers, Millstream Rd — re: item 4.1 — Speaker expressed concern with the CRD Arts and
     Culture program noting high costs. Speaker also noted that outreach to directly neighbouring
     municipalities is needed and could result in more programs locally rather than providing money
     to the City of Victoria. Speaker noted many programs locally such as the P.A.C.E program and

     programs available through organizations like the Y.M.C.A. Speaker expressed concern with the
     permanency of the agreement noting there is no opt-out feature.

     B. Armstrong, Rodney Rd — re: item 4.1 — Speaker noted that the CRD Arts and Culture program
     is a CRD initiative and not a City of Victoria one. Speaker expressed support for regional arts and
     culture noting many residents of Langford travel around the CRD. Speaker noted that currently
     there is a need to travel outside of the City to experience arts and culture. Speaker also noted
     interest in seeing a report regarding the program in the future.

     S. Rossander, Ravensview Dr — re: item 4.1— Speaker expressed support for a report being
     written exploring the pros and cons of joining the CRD Arts and Culture program. Speaker
     expressed opposition to joining the CRD Arts and Culture program noting the permanency of the
     agreement as there is no opt-out feature.

     L. Foxall, Players Dr — re: item 9.4 -- Speaker noted the minutes did not mention the
     repercussions of the social media clause, only the policies. re: item 4.1 — Speaker noted that they
     have received feedback from residents wishing not to partner with the City of Victoria. Speaker
     noted that the City partners with many neighbouring municipalities who share borders on
     numerous issues and in order to keep investment and jobs in the City, Langford should not
     partner with the CRD on this program. Speaker expressed concern with the permanency of the
     agreement as there is no opt-out feature. Speaker noted an arts and culture center could be
     built at the new university in partnership with nearby municipalities.

reservations.reason: Unique complete source occurrence identified using property/bylaw/permit/stage. Existing shortened wording and any ballot/manual evidence preserved; no full-text certification or new individual votes.

reservations.legacy_text:
THAT Council:

              1. That Royal Roads University allocate and disburse the annual $75,000 pledge
              payment from City of Langford per the Gift Agreement to each partnering post-
              secondary institution (Royal Roads University, University of Victoria, Camosun
              College, Justice Institute of BC) proportionately to their projected annual
              student enrolment numbers to programs available at the RRU Langford Campus.

              AND

              2. That the Langford Education Awards eligibility criteria focus on students who:

              a. Are 26 years or younger.

              b. Have graduated from a high school in School District 62 and resided in the City
              of Langford at the time of graduation.

              c. Are enrolled and are entering a Royal Roads University, University of Victoria,
              Camosun College, and/or Justice Institute of British Columbia program offered at
              the Royal Roads University Langford campus.

              d. Have demonstrated reasonable financial need.

              AND

              3. And that preference be given to students who self-identify as belonging to an
              under-represented group, including but not limited to: Indigenous, racialized,
              2SLGBTQQIA+, neuro-diverse, persons living with a visible or invisible disability,
              youth from care, and/or first in family to attend post-secondary.

              AND

              That the funds available provide student entrance awards with a maximum value
              of $10,000 to students as long as funds are available.
